body:
🤖 *This description was drafted by an AI agent (Claude Code).*

#### References to other Issues or PRs


#### Brief description of what is fixed or changed

Type annotations in `sympy/simplify/radsimp.py`:

- `fraction(expr: Expr, exact: bool = False) -> tuple[Expr, Expr]`
- `numer` and `denom`: same parameters, `-> Expr`
- In `fraction`, `term.is_Rational` becomes `isinstance(term, Rational)` so type checkers accept `term.p` and `term.q`. Only `Rational` sets `is_Rational = True`, so behavior is unchanged.

#### Other comments

`mypy sympy`, `ruff check sympy`, `bin/test quality`, `radsimp.py` doctests, and the radsimp/simplify tests pass locally.

#### AI Generation Disclosure

Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) wrote all changes in this PR and this description. Hunter Hogan reviewed them.

#### Release Notes

<!-- BEGIN RELEASE NOTES -->
* simplify
    * radsimp: Add types to `fraction`
<!-- END RELEASE NOTES -->

commits.author: Hunter Hogan
commits.message:
Annotate fraction, numer, and denom

fraction takes an Expr and returns a pair of Expr. Testing
isinstance(term, Rational) instead of term.is_Rational lets type
checkers see .p and .q; only Rational sets is_Rational.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Hunter Hogan
commits.message:
Accept unsympified input in fraction, numer, and denom

fraction sympifies its argument, so Expr | complex matches the convention
for parameters that have not been sympified yet.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Hunter Hogan
commits.message:
Declare fraction's numer and denom lists as Expr | int

Rational.p and Rational.q are int. Once @cacheit was typed, mypy inferred
list[Expr] for the lists and rejected appending them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Hunter Hogan
commits.message:
Narrow numer to Mul in LatexPrinter._print_Mul

fraction now returns Expr, so numer.args is tuple[Basic, ...]; with the
Integer.__mul__ overloads from #29422, a*x no longer type checks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

+                    b: Expr = S.One
                     for x in numer.args:
                         if self._needs_mul_brackets(x, last=False) or \
                                 len(convert(a*x).split()) > ratio*ldenom or \
diff --git a/sympy/simplify/radsimp.py b/sympy/simplify/radsimp.py
index 7945c691325b..c4699be19930 100644
--- a/sympy/simplify/radsimp.py
+++ b/sympy/simplify/radsimp.py
@@ -1,4 +1,5 @@
 from __future__ import annotations
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
 from collections import defaultdict
 
 from sympy.core import sympify, S, Mul, Derivative, Pow
@@ -17,7 +18,8 @@
 from sympy.simplify.sqrtdenest import sqrtdenest
 from sympy.utilities.iterables import iterable, sift
 
-
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from sympy.core.expr import Expr
 
 
 def collect(expr, syms, func=None, evaluate=None, exact=False, distribute_order_term=True):
@@ -1048,7 +1050,7 @@ def rad_rationalize(num, den):
     return rad_rationalize(num, den)
 
 
-def fraction(expr, exact=False):
+def fraction(expr: Expr | complex, exact: bool = False) -> tuple[Expr, Expr]:
     """Returns a pair with expression's numerator and denominator.
        If the given expression is not a fraction then this function
        will return the tuple (expr, 1).
@@ -1106,7 +1108,8 @@ def fraction(expr, exact=False):
     """
     expr = sympify(expr)
 
-    numer, denom = [], []
+    numer: list[Expr | int] = []
+    denom: list[Expr | int] = []
 
     for term in Mul.make_args(expr):
         if term.is_commutative and (term.is_Pow or isinstance(term, exp)):
@@ -1133,7 +1136,7 @@ def fraction(expr, exact=False):
                 denom.append(d)
             else:
                 numer.append(term)
-        elif term.is_Rational and not term.is_Integer:
+        elif isinstance(term, Rational) and not term.is_Integer:
             if term.p != 1:
                 numer.append(term.p)
             denom.append(term.q)
@@ -1142,11 +1145,11 @@ def fraction(expr, exact=False):
     return Mul(*numer, evaluate=not exact), Mul(*denom, evaluate=not exact)
 
 
-def numer(expr, exact=False):  # default matches fraction's default
+def numer(expr: Expr | complex, exact: bool = False) -> Expr:  # default matches fraction's default
     return fraction(expr, exact=exact)[0]
 
 
-def denom(expr, exact=False):  # default matches fraction's default
+def denom(expr: Expr | complex, exact: bool = False) -> Expr:  # default matches fraction's default
     return fraction(expr, exact=exact)[1]
